fix: Adopt as written. Start ladder_watch.py at ~03:30-03:45Z with --s0 experiments/e10_watch/20260927T0147Z.txt, under the PC14-02 restart loop with stdout redirected (--s0 is ignored once state.json holds S0). Record the S0 as a 01:47Z snapshot so the audit does not read it as a start-time baseline. Do not describe the earlier start as needed because exp70d will score around 04:05Z. Its real purpose is insurance and a lower risk of co-completion (count delta >= 2) at the first read. Optional: if 429s appear before 04:10Z, pause via the PAUSE file. There is no CLI flag to slow FAST_S (120 s) before the ladder's likely window.
realistic_gain: No score change. It protects the attribution machinery (L5v2 POS reads and the A-only exp70a extension, which is DROPPED if attribution fails) in the ~5-10% world where a ladder ref completes before 04:10Z, and in any world where the start-time baseline download fails. The downstream decision value is small (P(combo) ~0.01-0.03; the A-only swap needs 0.954 with an attributable UP), but the cost is zero.
